_comment: Worked example. Copy to guide-config.json and edit. All paths are relative to THIS config file. 'assistant_name' is the voice guide's name (chosen in Phase 0). 'avatar' is its portrait. 'audio_mode': 'url' lazy-loads audio/<file> (recommended, light); 'inline' base64-inlines the clips into one self-contained file. 'anchors' inject ids onto the leaflet's section heads so a segment can scroll/highlight to them (match the exact HTML string). 'segments' = the narration: text + the element it scrolls to (target null = top; block = scrollIntoView start|center). 'labels' overrides the widget's chrome strings per language (see _labels_comment); omit it entirely for English. BRAND: the widget inherits the PAGE's colours/font automatically — it reads --brand-* tokens via --guide-* (no re-tint pass). If your page changes --brand-primary, also set --guide-accent-rgb on the page so the aura/ring glow matches.
_labels_comment: i18n of the widget chrome. ENGLISH is the default — drop the whole 'labels' block for an English page. For another language, override only the keys you need. 'hear' uses {name} for the agent name. French example: { "ask": "Demander \u00e0", "resume": "Reprendre", "pause": "Pause", "dismiss": "Fermer", "reopen": "Rouvrir", "hear": "\u00c9couter {name} expliquer" }. The block below shows the English defaults explicitly so you can see every key.

segments.text: Hi, I'm Ava. Let me walk you through this service. It only takes a few steps, and I'll explain each one as we go.
First, what you need before you start: your identity document and a few details about your request. Have them ready and the rest is quick.
Here's how it works. You fill in the form, the system checks it, and an officer reviews it. You can follow the progress at every stage.
And at the end, this is what you receive. When you're ready, you can begin, and I'm here whenever you need me.
